analysis_status: effect-blind directional replication design frozen before dyad-level gain/loss effects were inspected

source.article: Dominguez-Garcia et al. 2026 Ecology Letters e70293

gain.interpretation: pooled axis difference is essentially zero and does not rescue the primary gain-direction mismatch

loss.interpretation: plant-side loss dominance persists when plant abundance replaces plant phenology

cross_system_read.supported: The Villavicencio plant-side dominance for link loss generalizes directionally to the independent 12-site system under out-of-site validation.
cross_system_read.not_supported: The Villavicencio pollinator-side dominance for link gain does not generalize under the pre-frozen external measurement: external gain discrimination is more plant-phenology weighted.
cross_system_read.revised_hypothesis: Plant-side availability may be a more general constraint on persistence/loss, whereas the dominant opportunity axis for link formation is system- or measurement-dependent rather than universal.
cross_system_read.importance: This narrows the ecological claim before any routeability interpretation: opportunity is reproducibly relevant, but the internal allocation of predictive information across plant and pollinator axes is not universally asymmetric in the same direction.

not_established: causal plant control of link loss
why the gain-side axis differs between systems
equivalence of measurement scales across datasets
claim_ceiling: External predictive-direction replication is mixed. The plant-side loss direction is cross-system consistent; the gain-side direction is not. Do not promote the Villavicencio gain-axis asymmetry to a universal assembly mechanism, and do not interpret either result as causal or as evidence for routeability.
